key_insight: OmniShotCut reconceptualizes shot-boundary detection as a structured relational prediction problem and uses a Shot‑Query Transformer to jointly model shot boundaries and inter-shot relations, improving interpretability and sensitivity to subtle transitions.
problem_solved: Existing SBD methods produce non‑interpretable boundaries, miss subtle but harmful discontinuities, and depend on noisy, low‑diversity annotations and outdated benchmarks.
method: Formulate SBD as holistic relational prediction—predict shot boundaries together with pairwise/relational shot structure instead of independent frame decisions.
Introduce a Shot‑Query Transformer that attends across temporal queries to capture long‑range and relational cues for boundary localization and transition type reasoning.
Reduce reliance on noisy labels by incorporating improved annotation/benchmarking and training strategies (better supervision and evaluation protocols) to yield more reliable, interpretable outputs.
impact: Provides a more interpretable, robust SBD approach that better detects subtle transitions and supports downstream video tasks (indexing, editing, retrieval) with cleaner shot segmentation and clearer failure modes for practitioners.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram of the Shot‑Query Transformer showing temporal queries, cross‑attention, and relational output heads (boundaries + relations).
Timeline/comparison strip showing ground‑truth shot, abrupt cut, dissolve, and a subtle discontinuity with model predictions overlaid.
Relational graph visualization linking shots (nodes) with predicted relations and boundary confidence (edge thickness/color).
Bar or precision‑recall chart comparing OmniShotCut vs. prior SOTA on fault types (abrupt, gradual, subtle discontinuities).
paper_title: OmniShotCut: Holistic Relational Shot Boundary Detection with Shot-Query Transformer
paper_authors: Boyang Wang, Guangyi Xu, Zhipeng Tang, Jiahui Zhang, Zezhou Cheng
